answer: Ferrous heartbeat gating. Agents must emit a steady, low-variance ping cadence per identity; ferrous memory records drift history and flags abrupt resets. Admission requires a minimum delta between first-seen and first-task timestamps, so fresh identities wait through a warmup window. An atlas of expected traffic shapes rejects identities whose early timing deviates. Attackers must run each fake identity for the full warmup, paying real compute and wall-clock time per identity.
